 28m ago 11.57 EST Trump landed in China on Wednesday seeking to reinforce America’s status as the world’s leading technology power, but a distressing series of technical outages back home has left his administration scrambling to calm the US public. 
 The issues put the administration on the defensive at a moment when the president wants to project strength and certainty before the meeting with Xi and Putin.
 As he began his trip to Asia, Trump initially had been nonchalant about the outages that left people in the US worried about accessing their email, checking their bank accounts or safely flying on an airplane.
 “It’s fine,” Trump said Tuesday from the Philippine capital of Manila, suggesting it was all just a consequence of being a nation that is “big and powerful.”
 Share Updated at  11.58 EST 2h ago 10.40 EST The meeting between the leaders of China , the United States and Russia planned for Thursday in Shenzhen is set to last less than 60 minutes, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian state media. 
 “No more than an hour” has been set aside for the historic summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin , Peskov was quoted as saying by Russian state news agencies.
 Share 2h ago 10.10 EST Rebecca Bailey The Associated Press is reporting that Donald Trump plans to hold a separate meeting with Vladimir Putin on Thursday, citing an anonymous US official. 
 The meeting would be in addition to the blockbuster trilateral talks the two will hold with host Xi Jinping on Thursday.
 If confirmed, it would be their first bilateral since they met in Alaska in 2025 for talks that failed to reach a deal on the war in Ukraine.
 Trump had already suggested he might meet with Putin, as well as with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, but neither option had been added to his official schedule.
 Share 3h ago 09.26 EST Trump treated to fried chicken by Philippines president
 Before landing in Shenzhen, Donald Trump enjoyed lunch in Manila with Philippine president Ferdinand Marcos Jr at the Malacañang presidential palace.
 Speaking during a meeting ahead of lunch, Marcos revealed that he had arranged for fried chicken from Filipino fast food chain Jollibee to be delivered to the US delegation as a late-night snack last night, praising Trump for “working very hard”.
 View image in fullscreen Donald Trump and Ferdinand Marcos Jr are joined by the Philippine first lady Louise Araneta-Marcos and US secretary of state Marco Rubio for lunch at the Malacañang presidential Palace in Manila on Wednesday. Photograph: Rolex dela Pena/Reuters The gift may have gone down particularly well with Trump, who has something of a reputation for his love of fast food. The US president has long been associated with McDonald’s and KFC, with his former campaign aides revealing in 2017 that his usual McDonald’s order included two Big Macs, two Filet-O-Fish sandwiches and a chocolate milkshake. The Guardian reported on their revelations at the time in this article:
 How to eat like a world leader: from Trump’s Big Macs to Thatcher’s Bovril toast Read more Share Updated at  09.28 EST 4h ago 08.54 EST Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum won praise and went viral on Chinese social media on Wednesday for taking an economy flight to attend a regional summit in Shenzhen. 
 World leaders this week descended on the southern Chinese city to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings – many arriving in specially chartered commercial airliners or dedicated government aircraft like US president Donald Trump’s Air Force One.
 Sheinbaum, however, flew in economy class from Mexico City to Shenzhen on a China Southern Airlines flight, media reports said. She arrived in China on Monday.
 Posts on Chinese social media platform Weibo showed the Mexican leader in the plane chatting with passengers, though the photos could not be independently verified by AFP. A hashtag on Weibo about her arrival in China garnered 10.2m views as of Wednesday.
 Meanwhile, Sheinbaum said ​on Wednesday she had a “very good ⁠meeting” with her US counterpart Trump ⁠as the two ​countries ‌pursue negotiations aimed ‌at easing trade tensions.
 “We ‌continue to make progress on our shared agenda,” Sheinbaum added in a post on ‌X.
 View image in fullscreen Prime Minister Mark Carney meets with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum in Shenzhen, China, Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026. Photograph: Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press/AP Share Updated at  08.57 EST 4h ago 08.19 EST View image in fullscreen (Back row, L-R) Papua New Guinea prime minister James Marape, New Zealand prime minister Christopher Luxon, Canadian prime minister Mark Carney, Australian prime minister Anthony Albanese, prime minister of Malaysia Anwar Ibrahim, Thailand’s prime minister Anutin Charnvirakul, his wife Sasithorn Chantarasomboon Singaporean prime minister Lawrence Wong, (Front row, C, L-R) US president Donald Trump, China’s president Xi Jinping, his wife Peng Liyuan, and Russian president Vladimir Putin pose for a group photo at the Apec summit banquet in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday. Photograph: Lukas Coch/EPA Share Updated at  09.02 EST 4h ago 07.59 EST Carney and Trump discuss trade deal in meeting on sidelines of Apec summit, PM's office says
 The Canadian prime minister’s office has issued a statement following Mark Carney’s meeting with US president Donald Trump on the sidelines of the Apec summit in Shenzhen.
 It said:
 double quotation mark This evening, the Prime Minister, Mark Carney, met with the President of the United States, Donald J. Trump, on the margins of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting, in Shenzhen, China.
 The leaders discussed the work underway to reach a mutually beneficial trade agreement that would create good jobs, boost affordability, and fully respect Canada’s languages, culture, and sovereignty. They agreed to continue the work and to stay in close contact.
 View image in fullscreen Canadian prime minister Mark Carney at the Apec banquet on Wednesday. Photograph: Maxim Shemetov/Pool Reuters/AP Share Updated at  08.00 EST 5h ago 07.27 EST Here is more of Xi’s speech (as per Xinhua):
 double quotation mark At tomorrow’s Leaders’ Meeting, we will discuss measures to expand mutual openness, explore pathways for innovation-driven growth, broaden opportunities for pragmatic cooperation in various fields, and promote the implementation of more outcomes. I look forward to discussing the grand plan for Asia-Pacific cooperation and jointly advancing the cause of Asia-Pacific development with you all.
 Now, I propose that we raise a glass together.
 For the common prosperity of the Asia-Pacific region,
 For the success of this informal leaders’ meeting,
 For the health of all guests and their families,
 Cheers!
 View image in fullscreen Xi Jinping raises a toast at the Apec welcome banquet. Photograph: Maxim Shemetov/Pool Reuters/AP Share Updated at  07.41 EST 5h ago 07.17 EST Xi hails Shenzhen's transformation in Apec banquet speech
 China’s state news agency Xinhua has published the text of Xi Jinping’s welcome speech at tonight’s Apec banquet in Shenzhen.
 In his remarks, Xi praised the city’s transformation into an international economic and innovation hub, describing it as a symbol of China’s development.
 Here are a few passages from his address:
 double quotation mark This evening, the shores of the South China Sea are aglow with lights, and autumn is in full swing here in Shenzhen, the City of the Phoenix. As the 33rd Apec Economic Leaders’ Meeting is about to commence, I would like, on behalf of the Chinese Government and the Chinese people, to extend a warm welcome to all our distinguished guests.
 I have often said that to see a thousand years of China, one should visit Xi’an; to see five hundred years of China, one should visit Beijing; and to see a hundred years of China, one should visit Shanghai. Today, I would like to say to you all: to see fifty years of China, come to Shenzhen.
 Shenzhen is a place with a rich history. In 1978, when I first came to Shenzhen, it was still a small fishing village. More than 40 years have passed in the blink of an eye, and now it is filled with high-rise buildings and bustling traffic. The changes are truly remarkable.”
 View image in fullscreen Chinese president Xi Jinping speaks at a welcome banquet for the Apec summit in Shenzhen, China. Photograph: Maxim Shemetov/AFP/Getty Images Share 6h ago 06.39 EST Trump and Putin shake hands ahead of Apec welcome banquet
